title: French Navy Seizes Sanctioned Russian Oil Tanker Tagor in Atlantic
detail: President Macron announced that the French Navy, with UK support, intercepted the sanctioned Russian oil tanker Tagor more than 400 nautical miles west of Brittany in international waters. The vessel had departed Murmansk and was operating under a false flag — having cycled through Marshall Islands, Madagascar, and Panama registrations — to circumvent EU sanctions on Russian crude exports financing the war in Ukraine. Macron called the tanker's activities 'unacceptable' and framed the seizure as part of France's commitment to enforcing sanctions on Russia. The Kremlin denounced the operation as 'illegal, bordering on international piracy.' It was France's third known interception of a Russian shadow-fleet vessel in recent months, reflecting a hardened European posture on sanctions enforcement.

media.caption: France seizes sanctioned Russian oil tanker Tagor in Atlantic — Macron announces third shadow-fleet interception

title: Austerity Plan Strikes Justice System and France 2030 Innovation Programme Hardest
detail: The French government's austerity plan is hitting the justice system and France 2030 innovation programme most severely, as budget cuts deepen across key public investment areas. The justice ministry faces significant reductions that threaten court staffing and prison capacity, while the flagship France 2030 industrial and technology investment programme — designed to reindustrialise France and fund green and digital transitions — faces painful cuts that risk undermining strategic economic priorities. The across-the-board spending reductions reflect the government's effort to narrow France's public deficit, which has persistently exceeded EU fiscal rules.
